claims.explanation: Azathioprine is a prodrug of 6-mercaptopurine that requires HPRT1-mediated conversion to active thioguanine nucleotides, which are incorporated into DNA and inhibit de novo purine synthesis via IMPDH and PPAT; selectivity likely reflects dependence on purine salvage and nucleotide metabolism, with TP53-mutant and RAS/MAPK-activated lines showing increased sensitivity due to impaired DNA damage response and altered nucleotide demand. Lines with intact DNA damage checkpoints or low HPRT1 expression are relatively protected.

features.basis: Required for azathioprine activation to thioguanine nucleotides
Loss of DNA damage response increases sensitivity to thiopurine-induced DNA incorporation
Oncogenic RAS increases nucleotide demand and sensitivity to purine synthesis inhibition
MAPK pathway activation increases proliferation and purine dependency
High IMPDH1 may compensate for azathioprine-mediated inhibition of de novo purine synthesis
High PPAT may bypass azathioprine inhibition of purine synthesis
PI3K activation increases proliferation and nucleotide demand
Loss of NF1 activates RAS/MAPK, increasing purine dependency
Cell cycle checkpoint loss increases sensitivity to DNA incorporation
Impaired DNA damage response increases thiopurine cytotoxicity
PTEN loss may reduce dependence on purine salvage and increase resistance
EGFR-mutant lung lines were among least affected, suggesting reduced sensitivity
